what_happened: Job 20261103-075205-wbtm ("Render owner decision briefs from open Steward proposals on the site") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic confirmed that the APIs and seams the plan names exist, that no new dependency is needed, and that the demonstrations use real fixtures. One major finding remained. The plan's recommendation rule guesses the raising role's limit, though that limit can be read from role records through athena-data. athena-core's split_open approves in-limit proposals without a person. So the 'Decide yourself' line can be false for proposals at the design-decisions and defaults-conventions rungs. There was one minor finding: the stated run command misses one of the three tests the demonstration for criterion 8 relies on. There was also one nit: the plan never says which GitHub base the records links use. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist. It does not require the plan to settle design questions that the code can answer. The plan took a heuristic, a guess at the role's limit, and left it as an open question and a rejected alternative. Reading the role records, or the existing split_open path that already encodes the approval rule, would have settled it. Nothing makes the plan trace a derived output (the recommendation) back to the rule the system already applies to the same data. Planning has three fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan, and has no repair step for a defect the code could answer. So a gap the critic finds in round 3 loses all the planning spend.
prevention: Add a planning rule, enforced by code, that every open question and every 'rejected alternative' resting on a guess is checked against the snapshot before the critic's first round. Questions about a value or rule that existing code or records already hold must be resolved in the plan, with the cited source. Plans that derive a user-facing recommendation from system data must reuse the function that already applies the rule (here split_open and the role limit read from records) rather than approximate it. Add a bounded repair round after the last critic round for findings that are only mechanical or code-answerable, so a single major finding of this kind does not fail the job with no plan kept.
proposed_request: Render owner decision briefs from open Steward proposals on the site. For each open proposal, the site page shows a brief that includes the proposal, its links into the records, its state, and a recommendation. Outcome: the recommendation must match what the system would do. A proposal within the raising role's limit is approved without a person, so the brief must not say 'Decide yourself' for it. A proposal above the limit does need the owner, so the brief says so. Derive the role's limit by reading the role records through athena-data and reuse the same rule athena-core's split_open applies. Do not guess or hard-code limits per rung. Use the records branch and tracking ref through the existing resolve_tip and Git helpers. State which GitHub base the records links use, and take it from the existing site::source_url logic. Cover with tests on real fixtures: a proposal in limit, one above the limit, one with an absent field, and the link and page states. Make sure the stated run command runs every test the demonstrations rely on. Add a CHANGELOG entry. Do not add new dependencies.
